subject: Post-demo: DataHarbor retention & PII handling — next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna@dataharbor.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:12:00-05:00
Subject: Post-demo: DataHarbor retention & PII handling — next steps

Anna — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps while they're fresh: 

Key takeaways from our call:
- DataHarbor needs assurance that user-identifying PII and PHI will not be retained beyond the inference request lifecycle unless explicitly permitted.
- You prefer: 0-retention for PII (user IDs, email, SSNs), short-lived KV for session context, and EU/US residency for model execution.
- Procurement will need an addendum to the MSA covering retention, BYOK, and SOC2 evidence.

Proposed immediate next steps: 
1) Can you confirm the specific PII fields you want treated as zero-retention (e.g., user_id, email, date_of_birth, phone)? Reply with a short list so we align technical controls.
2) Would you accept pseudonymization/hash-on-ingest (customer-side) + BYOK for any keys that touch PII?
3) I'll loop in Privacy (Stephanie) and Solutions (Grace) to propose an exception pathway and a short pilot (7–14 days) to validate end-to-end behavior.

I've attached a short PDF that outlines our configurable retention options and a CSV with an initial proposed TTL schedule. If procurement is available, let's schedule a 30-min procurement/technical sync next week — suggest Wed 11/11 or Thu 11/12.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-data-retention-options.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: marcus-proposed-ttl.csv (csv)

From: Anna Patel <anna@dataharbor.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T17:08:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: DataHarbor retention & PII handling — next steps

Marcus — thanks for the recap and the materials. Quick clarifications from our security & product teams: 

PII scope we want treated as zero-retention unless specifically covered by a signed, explicit data processing addendum:
- direct_user_identifiers: user_id, email, phone_number
- auth_identifiers: auth_token (transient), federated_id
- sensitive_attributes: national_id, SSN, full DOB, health symptom descriptions when submitted as free text

We are open to customer-side pseudonymization/hashing, but it must be deterministic (we need to be able to correlate cross-requests internally), and keys must never leave our control (BYOK/HSM).

Questions for Redwood: 
- Can you guarantee no server-side persistent storage of the above PII fields (0-retention), including in any debugging logs or traces, without an addendum?
- For session context (KV cache) we can tolerate very short-lived state during inference — what's the minimum TTL Redwood can commit to for KV?
- What evidence can you provide for SOC 2 / controls and for key custody (BYOK) — is there a standard addendum you use?

Procurement looped me in (procurement@dataharbor.ai) — they want to see the proposed addendum language and estimated uplift for a private retention exception. They're available Thu 11/12 afternoon.

— Anna
Anna Patel
Head of Product Security | DataHarbor
anna@dataharbor.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Anna Patel <anna@dataharbor.ai>, DataHarbor Procurement <procurement@dataharbor.ai>
Date: 2026-11-11T09:35:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: DataHarbor retention & PII handling — next steps

Stephanie / Grace — forwarding Anna's reply and procurement availability. High level ask from DataHarbor: 0-retention for enumerated PII + BYOK/HSM and a short KV TTL for session context. Procurement wants ballpark uplift for an exception addendum and a short call Thu 11/12 afternoon.

My proposed technical compromise (for your review) — trying to be conservative while keeping the deal moving: 
- PII fields (as Anna enumerated) — 0-retention at rest on Redwood side. No persistent storage in logs, traces, or debug endpoints.
- Session KV: strict ephemeral KV with an initial pilot TTL = 48 hours (to allow debugging); production target TTL = 4 hours.
- Aggregated telemetry (non-PII): 30-day rolling retention for model quality metrics (token-level hashes only).
- Audit evidence: supply SOC2 Type II report + architecture diagram showing key paths. Offer technical runbook for the pilot.
- Keys: BYOK via customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys; Redwood supports AWS KMS/HSM and can accept external wrapped keys.

Attachments: marcus-proposed-ttl.csv (csv) outlines the above schedule and a short note on fallback behavior when the KV is not present.

Can Privacy (Stephanie) confirm if the 0-retention + BYOK approach is acceptable from a compliance standpoint, and whether we should offer an explicit 7-day pilot window instead of 48 hours to help DataHarbor validate integration?

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Anna Patel <anna@dataharbor.ai>, DataHarbor Procurement <procurement@dataharbor.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T10:06:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: DataHarbor retention & PII handling — next steps

Thanks for the context, Marcus, and hi Anna — appreciate the clear list. High-level from Privacy & Compliance: we can support a limited, documented exception path subject to an addendum and a short technical pilot. Summary of what Redwood can formalize: 

1) PII handling
- Redwood will not persist the enumerated PII fields at rest on Redwood-managed storage or in long-term logs. Any PII that reaches our endpoints must be redacted or hashed before being written to persistent storage.
- We support deterministic, customer-side pseudonymization as a preferred pattern; if customer elects this, keys must remain under customer control and be provisioned via BYOK (AWS KMS or equivalent HSM).

2) KV/session TTL (pilot & production)
- Pilot: 7-day TTL for KV (to give DataHarbor time to validate end-to-end). This pilot TTL is isolated to a dedicated test pool and flagged for immediate deletion after pilot validation.
- Production target: commit to configurable TTLs with a default of 4 hours for session KV for any approved customers under the exception addendum.

3) Logs, traces, and debug endpoints
- Redwood will implement a scrub policy: by default, request-level logs do not contain raw PII fields; we will provide a tokenized trace id and aggregate metrics. Any request-level debugging snapshots require explicit, time-bound consent from the customer and are captured only in the test pilot with immediate purge after troubleshooting.

4) Evidence & addendum
- We'll provide SOC 2 Type II report (redacted as needed), architecture diagrams, and a standard retention addendum draft. The addendum will declare the custom TTLs and BYOK terms; pricing uplift will be provided by Sales + Finance after procurement confirms scope.

Next steps (recommended):
- Marcus: send the proposed addendum draft and proposed pilot timeline to procurement.
- Anna / Procurement: confirm participants and preferred Thu 11/12 3:00–3:30pm ET for a short procurement + privacy sync.
- Grace: prepare a short runbook for the pilot that documents how to provision BYOK, how to enable client-side pseudonymization, and the deletion verification steps.

If procurement needs preliminary pricing, Sales can provide a banded uplift estimate; final pricing requires signed addendum. Happy to join the Thu call.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com
